13.0.s.en: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

13.0.0.en: Joshua had become a very old man, perhaps 107 years of age. He had spent seven years of them in his wars to possess the land of Canaan, and he had only three years of life left, for he would die at the age of 110 (ch. 24:29). So God drew his attention to the many lands in Canaan that God had given them and that they had not yet fought for and possessed, and that they must complete the possession of these lands.

13.1.1.en: Before Egypt: east of Egypt and facing it.

13.1.4.en: The lands that remained and that the children of Israel had not yet possessed are:

13.1.5.en: 1- All the borders of the Philistines: that is, the region surrounding the southeast of the Mediterranean Sea, in which the Philistines lived, who are descended from Ham and are counted among the Canaanites.

13.1.6.en: 2- The lands of the Geshurites: which lie in the south of Palestine, west of the Jordan, and are different from the land of the Geshurites that lies east of the Jordan and was possessed by the eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh in the days of Moses (ch. 12:5).

13.1.7.en: 3- The great cities of Palestine, which begin from Sihor, a seasonal river lying east of Egypt and called the Wadi al-Arish, as far as the city of Ekron in the north; and they include five cities:

13.1.8.en: a- Gaza: it is the southern border of Palestine. The tribe of Judah possessed it (Judg 1:18), and the Philistines recovered it, then the Maccabees possessed it (1 Macc 13:43-48).

13.1.9.en: b- Ashdod: a fortified city, hence it was given this name, that is, strengthened and strong, and the Maccabees possessed it (1 Macc 5:68, 10:84).

13.1.10.en: c- Ashkelon: it lies 12 miles north of Gaza and is now called Asqalan.

13.1.11.en: d- Gath: a fortified city taken by David, then Rehoboam, and after him Jehoash (2 Sam 15:18, 2 Chr 11:8, 2 Kgs 13:25).

13.1.12.en: e- Ekron: it is the northern border of these cities and lies about 12 miles south of Joppa. God's people possessed it in the days of Joshua (ch. 15:45) and then in the days of Samuel (1 Sam 7:14), but afterwards the Philistines took it (Map 6).

13.1.13.en: 4- The Avites: who lived near Gaza and were counted among the Philistines and then among the Canaanites. Joppa, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, Palestine, Gaza. Map (6)

13.2.1.en: He continues the lands that the children of Israel had not possessed, saying that the land extends southward to include the homeland of all the Canaanite tribes, then northward from the cave of the Sidonians, in whose mountain there are many caves, and they reached the city of Aphek, which lies north of Sidon in Libnah. The ancient land of the Amorites was south of Jerusalem, and some of them migrated to the east of the Jordan; their kings were Sihon and Og, and the children of Israel also possessed their country that was east of the Jordan (Num 21).

13.3.0.en: He also adds to the lands that they had not possessed the two mountains. The land of the Giblites lies 30 kilometers north of Beirut, and it is a Phoenician land, that is, Lebanon. It is the northern border of the land that God wished to give to His people; they are not Canaanites. As for Hamath, it lies north of Damascus in Syria. And Baal-gad is Caesarea Philippi, or Baalbek in Lebanon.

13.4.0.en: And the land of the inhabitants of the mountains, from Misrephoth beside Sidon to the border of Lebanon. The Lord promises to drive them out Himself before the Jews, to clear the land for them, on condition that Joshua divide it to them by lot, so that Joshua would not be accused of favoring any of the tribes.

13.5.0.en: The nine tribes, in addition to the half tribe of Manasseh, take their possession in this land, because the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh had taken their possession east of the Jordan in the days of Moses (Num 32).

13.5.1.en: We must be content with what the Lord has given us of spiritual and material gifts and blessings, and not accuse circumstances or others of favoritism and of standing against us, but invest what we have received without murmuring.

13.5.2.en: (2) The portions east of the Jordan (vv. 8-14:) 8 With whom the Reubenites and the Gadites have received their inheritance, which Moses gave them, beyond Jordan eastward, even as Moses the servant of the Lord gave them; 9 From Aroer, that is upon the bank of the river Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the river, and all the plain of Medeba unto Dibon; 10 And all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, which reigned in Heshbon, unto the border of the children of Ammon; 11 And Gilead, and the border of the Geshurites and Maachathites, and all mount Hermon, and all Bashan unto Salcah; 12 All the kingdom of Og in Bashan, which reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei, who remained of the remnant of the giants: for these did Moses smite, and cast them out. 13 Nevertheless the children of Israel expelled not the Geshurites, nor the Maachathites: but the Geshurites and the Maachathites dwell among the Israelites until this day. 14 Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the Lord God of Israel made by fire are his inheritance, as he said unto them.

13.6.0.en: With whom: with the rest of the tribes that took possession west of the Jordan, the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh took possession east of the Jordan.

13.6.1.en: Moses gave this land to the tribe of Reuben in the south, Gad in the middle, and the half tribe of Manasseh in the north, but they crossed over to fight with the rest of the people in the west, and they did not settle in it until the wars had ended and Joshua handed it over to them.

13.7.0.en: Aroer: it lies on the Arnon River, on the southern border of the kingdom of Sihon.

13.7.1.en: The city that is in the midst of the valley: what is meant is Heshbon or Arnon.

13.7.2.en: The plain of Medeba: it lies 14 miles east of the Dead Sea, and around it are many lakes.

13.7.3.en: Dibon: north of the Arnon River, at a distance of 3 miles.

13.7.4.en: Heshbon: it lies between the Arnon and Jabbok rivers and was the capital of King Sihon.

13.7.5.en: He defines the land east of the Jordan with its cities, mountains and rivers, from the Dead Sea and the border of Moab in the south to the border of the Ammonites in the east, and the border of Bashan alongside the Sea of Tiberias in the north. King Og was of the descendants of a people called the Rephaim (Maps 5, 7). Ashtaroth, Jericho. Map (7)

13.8.0.en: But the people did not carry out the commandment of Moses to drive out the rest of the pagan peoples such as the Geshurites and the Maachathites; rather they left them among them, either out of fear of them or out of a desire that they serve them as slaves and pay them tribute.

13.9.0.en: No land was given to the tribe of Levi; rather the rest of the tribes gave it cities for dwelling only (Num 35), as will be mentioned later, so that they would be spread out among the people to serve them spiritually, and so as not to be occupied with ownership at the expense of spiritual work. They lived from their share that they took from the sacrifices, that is, the offerings presented in the house of the Lord.

13.9.1.en: Do not be lax with evil, and do not let any image or form of it remain with you after your repentance, as the children of Israel were lax and did not drive out the pagan peoples living among them, because the devil is ready to lie in wait and be silent for a time, then return to attack you; so do not give him an opportunity.

13.9.2.en: (3) The portion of the tribe of Reuben (vv. 15-23:) 15 And Moses gave unto the tribe of the children of Reuben inheritance according to their families. 16 And their coast was from Aroer, that is on the bank of the river Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the river, and all the plain by Medeba; 17 Heshbon, and all her cities that are in the plain; Dibon, and Bamothbaal, and Bethbaalmeon, 18 And Jahaza, and Kedemoth, and Mephaath, 19 And Kirjathaim, and Sibmah, and Zarethshahar in the mount of the valley, 20 And Bethpeor, and Ashdothpisgah, and Bethjeshimoth, 21 And all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, which reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses smote with the princes of Midian, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, which were dukes of Sihon, dwelling in the country. 22 Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them. 23 And the border of the children of Reuben was Jordan, and the border thereof. This was the inheritance of the children of Reuben after their families, the cities and the villages thereof.

13.10.1.en: Villages thereof: the farms and villages belonging to the large city.

13.10.2.en: Bamoth-baal: a city lying north of the Arnon River and south of Mount Nebo (Num 21:19, 22:21), and the meaning of its name is the heights of Baal.

13.10.4.en: Beth-baal-meon: it lies a few miles south of Heshbon.

13.10.5.en: Jahaza: a city lying twelve miles east of the Dead Sea. Kedemoth: it lies in the valley of the Arnon River.

13.10.6.en: Kirjathaim: about two and a half miles north of the Arnon River.

13.10.7.en: Sibmah: it lies beside Heshbon, at a distance of two miles.

13.10.8.en: Zareth-shahar: it lies east of the Dead Sea at the mouth of the Zarqa River.

13.10.9.en: Beth-peor: that is, the temple of Peor, where the house and altar of Baal-peor were, beside the top of Pisgah (Deut 4:

13.10.10.en: 46.(The plains of Pisgah: one of the peaks of the mountains of Abarim, which lie northeast of the Dead Sea (Deut 34:1). Beth-jeshimoth: it lies northeast of the Dead Sea at the mouth of the Jordan River into the sea (Num 33:49). The cities of the plain: the plain lying between the Arnon and Jabbok rivers.

13.10.11.en: The princes of Sihon: the allies of King Sihon and his helpers, because the land of Midian was adjacent to King Sihon.

13.10.12.en: Jordan and the border thereof: that is, the lands lying east of the Jordan River.

13.10.13.en: The borders of the portion of the tribe of Reuben are Moab in the south, the portion of the tribe of Gad in the north, the Ammonites in the east, and the Dead Sea in the west, including the cities and villages in it (Maps 5, 7). Here is mentioned Balaam the son of Beor, whom Balak king of Moab hired to curse the Jews, but God blessed them, and the Jews killed him when they took possession of the land (Num 22-25).

13.10.14.en: Evil always returns upon the one who does it: Balaam's counsel, by which he caused the children of Israel to fall into adultery and idol worship, turned into the destruction of Balaam himself. So beware of giving bad counsel, or of having a personal aim and benefit in your guidance of others. That is, be careful to proclaim the voice of God and not your own thoughts.

13.10.15.en: (4) The portion of the tribe of Gad (vv. 24-28:) 24 And Moses gave inheritance unto the tribe of Gad, even unto the children of Gad according to their families. 25 And their coast was Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon, unto Aroer that is before Rabbah; 26 And from Heshbon unto Ramathmizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim unto the border of Debir; 27 And in the valley, Betharam, and Bethnimrah, and Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, Jordan and his border, even unto the edge of the sea of Chinnereth on the other side Jordan eastward. 28 This is the inheritance of the children of Gad after their families, the cities, and their villages.

13.11.0.en: Jazer: a city with fertile land in Gilead (Num 21:32). Rabbah: the city of Amman, the present capital of Jordan.

13.11.1.en: Ramath-mizpeh: it is Ramoth in Gilead (Deut 4:43). Mahanaim: it lies east of the Jordan River.

13.11.3.en: Beth-aram: it lies in the region of the plains of Moab.

13.11.4.en: Beth-nimrah: it lies east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho.

13.11.5.en: Succoth: it lies about a mile south of the Jabbok River.

13.11.6.en: Samon: it lies eight miles northeast of the mouth of the Jabbok River.

13.11.7.en: The sea of Chinnereth: it is the Lake of Gennesaret, or the Sea of Galilee, or Lake Tiberias, through which the Jordan River passes (Num 34:11). The portion of the tribe of Gad lay between the portion of the half tribe of Manasseh in the north and the portion of the tribe of Reuben in the south, and the rest of the land of the Ammonites in the east, after the sons of Gad took from the Amorites the land that the Amorites had earlier taken from the Ammonites; as for the western border of their portion, it is the Jordan River (Map 5).

13.11.8.en: God has prepared for you a portion in the Kingdom of Heaven. I wish you would take care to prepare for it so as to attain it and rejoice in it with God, and not be distracted from it by the passing concerns of the world; that is, set limits to your concerns and give sufficient time to your relationship with God.

13.11.9.en: (5) The portion of the half tribe of Manasseh (vv. 29-33:) 29 And Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh: and this was the possession of the half tribe of the children of Manasseh by their families.

13.11.10.en: 30 And their coast was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair, which are in Bashan, threescore cities: 31 And half Gilead, and Ashtaroth, and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were pertaining unto the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even to the one half of the children of Machir by their families. 32 These are the countries which Moses did distribute for inheritance in the plains of Moab, on the other side Jordan, by Jericho, eastward. 33 But unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave not any inheritance: the Lord God of Israel was their inheritance, as he said unto them.

13.12.0.en: Machir: the only son of Manasseh, and half of his descendants lived east of the Jordan and the other half west of it (Num 26:29, 1 Chr 7:14). The land of Bashan: it is the one ruled by Og (Num 21:31-35). Towns: farms, and what is meant is the agricultural cities and villages that Jair the son of Manasseh conquered.

13.12.1.en: Jair: he was of the tribe of Judah but was ascribed to the tribe of Manasseh because he married a woman of the descendants of Machir.

13.12.2.en: Half Gilead: the tribe of Manasseh took possession of it, and the other half was taken by the Reubenites and the Gadites.

13.12.3.en: Ashtaroth: a capital of the kingdom of Og, lying east of the Sea of Galilee at a distance of 21 miles (Num 21:33). Edrei: another capital of King Og, lying southeast of the Sea of Galilee at a distance of 29 miles (Num 21:33). To the one half of the children of Machir: because the other half took its portion near the Jordan.

13.12.4.en: The portion of the half tribe of Manasseh, who are of the descendants of Machir, was from the land of Bashan, good for pasture, in the north to the portion of the tribe of Gad in the south, and from the north of the land of Ammon in the east to the Jordan River and the Lake of Tiberias in the west (Map 7). The cities of the sons of Levi were distributed throughout the whole land, as mentioned before, and they took them only to dwell in, but they did not possess a portion of the lands like the rest of the tribes, because they were consecrated to the service of God, so their portion was the Lord, and this is the greatest thing.

13.12.5.en: God cares for those consecrated to His service and provides for them. And if you offer service to God, be confident that He blesses you spiritually and materially and cares for your needs, because you have become one of His servants and His special followers.

14.0.s.en: (1) The general division of the land

14.0.0.en: These: it refers to the lands that the children of Israel possessed west of the Jordan.

14.0.1.en: The distribution of the land took place in the presence of Eleazar the priest, the third son of Aaron, and Joshua, whom Moses had appointed ruler over the people, and likewise the heads of the tribes, one from each tribe. The name of Eleazar is put before Joshua here because Moses had ordained him ruler over the people in the presence of Eleazar the priest.

14.1.0.en: The distribution of the portions was by lot: the names of the tribes were written down and the portions were written down, and one was drawn from each, so that the portion was determined (Num 26:53, 33:54, 55). As for the Levites, they did not take a portion of the land; rather the Lord would give them cities to dwell in among the rest of the tribes (ch. 13:14, 33).

14.2.1.en: Their substance: their servants and their sheep.

14.2.2.en: Joseph became two tribes, and so the tribe of Levi had no portion. In this way Joseph enjoyed a double portion, which is the portion of the firstborn with regard to his father Jacob, and so the words of Moses were carried out in dividing the lands among the tribes.

14.2.3.en: Joseph's receiving two tribes and his being counted the firstborn of Jacob instead of Reuben was because Joseph was righteous, whereas Reuben sinned with his father's concubine and lost the blessing (Gen 35:21). So the tribes numbered twelve, because the Levites did not take a portion, and Joseph took their place by receiving two tribes, and the Levites took from each tribe cities to dwell in, with fields and pastures around them for their flocks, as mentioned in (Num 35).

14.2.4.en: The blessing of the Lord is great for the one who fears Him, like Joseph. So enjoy your relationship with God; then He provides all your needs, and even blesses you more than you imagine, and you rejoice in His fellowship.

14.3.0.en: The Kenezite: the Kenezites are a Canaanite tribe, from which Caleb may have come and become a Jew, or one of his ancestors was called Kenaz and was of Jewish origin.

14.3.1.en: Gilgal: a region south of Jericho lying on the Dead Sea, which was Joshua's headquarters (Map 1). Caleb came forward with a group from the tribe of Judah to Joshua; Caleb was the head of the tribe of Judah (Num 34:19), and a group of them came with him to support him in his request. Caleb reminded Joshua of Moses' praise of them both when they returned from spying out the land, and their encouraging the people to enter it, and of his promise to them of a portion in the land. It is understood from this that they had a distinction in the possession of the land because of their obedience to God and their encouraging the people (Num 13, 14).

14.4.0.en: Caleb was 40 years old when he went with Joshua from Kadesh to spy out the land, and he returned and testified truthfully to the greatness of God's promise to His people of this splendid land, for it is a land full of good things and God is able to lead His people and give them possession of this land.

14.5.0.en: Made melt: disturbed and terrified the children of Israel.

14.5.1.en: As for the rest of the spies, besides Caleb and Joshua, they turned aside from the way of God and frightened the people from entering the land of Canaan because of the strength of those who lived in it.

14.6.0.en: When Caleb spied out the land of Canaan, he entered the region of Hebron, that is, his feet trod upon it, and Moses promised him on his return from spying that he would take this land.

14.7.0.en: Thirty-eight years passed in the journey in the wilderness and seven years in the wars of Canaan with Joshua, and Caleb reached the age of 85.

14.8.0.en: Caleb had reached the age of 85, which is an advanced age, but his piety and love of God gave him a spiritual zeal that strengthened his body, so that he was ready for war and for possessing the land like any young man, that is, as he was in his strength at the age of 40 when he spied out the land.

14.9.0.en: The mountain: what is meant is the city of Hebron and the mountainous region surrounding it.

14.9.1.en: The Anakim: one of the tribes of Canaan, distinguished by tall stature and strength.

14.9.2.en: Thou heardest: the spies' frightening of the people so that the people would not enter it, because of the strength of its inhabitants, the Anakim and other tribes of Canaan.

14.9.3.en: Therefore he asks for his portion in the high mountain that the Anakim inhabited, so that he may drive them out and dwell in their place according to God's promise to him.

14.10.0.en: Hebron is the city of Al-Khalil, in which the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and their wives are buried. It became Caleb's possession, but he afterwards gave it up, and it became one of the cities of the Levites (Josh 21:13).

14.11.0.en: Hebron was first called Kirjath-arba, and Arba was the father of Anak, to whom the Anakim are ascribed; then Caleb changed its name to Hebron, after one of his descendants.

14.11.1.en: As a result of the peoples' fear of the Jews, they ceased to stir up war with them, and the land had rest.

14.11.2.en: Take courage in your spiritual striving, for you have a great portion of blessing with Christ. Fight by the grace of God and you will triumph and rejoice. Leave your sins and persevere in your striving to acquire virtue, knowing that you will triumph by the power of Christ.

14.11.3.en: The portion of the tribe of Judah. From here begins the distribution of the portions of three diligent tribes, namely the tribe of Judah (ch. 15), the tribe of Ephraim (ch. 16) and the half tribe of Manasseh (ch. 17). This distribution took place at Gilgal, and we begin with the portion of the tribe of Judah.
